pages: Orrin's student! Look at you, all elbows and ink. Sit down before you fall down.
The Lantern's beds are dry and the stew is mostly turnip. Rest here and I'll keep your place.
Lose a duel out there and they'll carry you back to me. They always do. Mind your purse when they do.
Late, isn't it? The stew's gone to glue and the fire's down to sulking. Sit anyway.
Hear the dogs? Every night since the hall went dark. They howl at the chapel, never the moor.
The dogs have stopped. First quiet night in a week, and I can't sleep for listening to it.
A bed's a bed, scribe. Take one. The road will still be there at dawn.
The coast, is it? Salt in your boots and fish in every pot. I'll pack you bread that won't drown.
Bring Orrin home. He owes me for eleven years of suppers, and I mean to collect.
Brann's lit the hall! I saw the windows from my kitchen and burned the bread for staring.
Hesk's been asking for you. Go on. Then come back and eat something.
You smell like the mill cellar. I won't ask what you trod in. Boots by the door.
Rest a while. Whatever's down there has waited this long. It can wait for supper.
Hesk sent you to the old mill? That man would send his own mother if she had a deck.
Rest first. A tired scribe draws bad cards. Orrin always said that, and he was always tired.
Fire's lit, stew's on. Rest your bones and I'll mark you down as staying.
Three nights since the hall went dark. Every night the dogs howl at the chapel.
Eh? A customer? Come closer, the light's poor and so are my eyes.
Singles, all sorted. Well, sorted by how I feel about them. You'll find the counter. Everyone does.
Open? I'm always open. Sleep is for people whose cards don't whisper.
They're louder after dark. Something under the mill talks to them. Buy one. Shut it up.
Quiet night. My cards are asleep. First time in years. I keep checking they're breathing.
A map of Orrin's? He drew me one once. To his house. I still got lost.
Off to the coast, then. Buy something with fins on it. They like that sort of thing there.
Hall's lit again. My cards stopped whispering. They whispered, you know. Forget I said so.
Good for trade, a lit hall. Duelists come back. Duelists buy.
Under the mill, eh? Echoes go strange in the dark. Take something cheap and stubborn.
A card that won't die is worth three that hit hard. I learned that at your age. Or Orrin's.
The Grave Priest? Used to buy black-edged cards from me. Paid in old coin. Smelled of lilies.
Should've known. Nobody honest smells of lilies.
Mind the stacks. That pile's in order. That one too. Don't touch that one, it bites.
Every card here has a story. Most of them are about me losing.
Sealed bundles, fresh from Brackwater. Nobody knows what's inside. That's the charm.
Wendel sells you what you want. I sell you hope. Hope costs a little more.
Night trade. Same packs, same prices, worse lighting. Some say the luck's better after dark.
I say that. I'm some.
Still up? Me too. A shopkeeper who sleeps misses the customers who can't.
Saltmere has a pack shop. Small, damp, dear. Say Ysolde sent you. They'll charge double.
Kidding. Mostly. Bring me back a coastal bundle and we'll call it even.
You beat the Priest? Then your luck's running hot. Never waste a hot hand. Open something.
I'm not saying that because I sell packs. I'm saying it because it's true and I sell packs.
Back in one piece. Good. Dead customers don't come back, whatever the Priest says.
A fresh bundle before you go down again? You never know what's sleeping in the wrappers.
Going after the Priest on the cards you've got? Brave. Or broke. Usually both.
A bundle or two might find you an answer. Might not. I don't do refunds on fate.
Packs, sealed and honest. The wrappers are honest, anyway.
Somebody opened three in a row last week and found the same card thrice. Swore at me. Not my fault.
Brackwater's stall, as far inland as I'll drag it. The town itself is three wet days east.
Blue and black, mostly. Cards that think, cards that drown things. Have a look.
Still trading. The lamp keeps the bandits honest. Mostly it keeps me awake.
Brackwater's stall. Fresh off the cart, a bit damp. Have a look.
Cinder Gate's stall. The road south goes to the Gate, if your boots can take the heat.
Black and red, all of it. Cards that burn and cards that bite. Have a look.
Night's no trouble. Anything that crawls out of the moor, I sell it a fire.
Cinder Gate's stall. Mind the coals. Have a look.
Who's there? Ah. Orrin's scribe. Mind the benches. I can't light the candles.
Three nights now. Strike a flame in here and it dies before it catches. Like the hall forgot how.
By the Accord, no quarrel here can be settled while this hall is dark. Think on that.
Orrin's scribe. You're the one who lit my candles, then, by beating that wretch.
The hall is open again. Come back when you want a duel. I keep the old challengers' decks.
Night or day, it's all one in here now. I sit with the benches so they don't feel forgotten.
The candles burn all night now. This hall won't forget again. Not while I live.
The hall stands lit, and the Accord with it. Any quarrel can be settled here again.
Want a rematch? I'll play you any foe you've beaten, deck for deck. Practice before the coast.
Look at it. Every candle, at once, the moment he fell. I wept. Don't tell Marta.
The hall is yours to use. And Hesk will want to see whatever you took off that Priest.
You've been below. I can tell. The dark sticks to a duelist like wet wool.
The Priest's Echoes are hollow. Hushed. They hit hard but they don't remember why. Outlast them.
Hesk sent you after the Priest. Good. The old fool is right for once.
Bring his Echoes to silence and I'll light this hall for you myself. If it lets me.
Dark as a well in here. Sit if you like. Mind the third bench, it's cracked.
Talk to Elder Hesk in the square. If anyone knows what put out these candles, it's him.
Halt. Who goes. Oh, it's you. Sorry. I say that to everyone. The sergeant likes it.
East road runs to the moor and the old mill. Bandits on it, thorn-beasts off it. Stay on it. Mostly.
Heard you're for the coast. Lucky. Nobody's for anywhere from this gate. I'm for this gate.
If you see my cousin in Saltmere, tell him he still owes me a hat.
No dead on the road last night. First time in a week. I nearly slept. On duty. Don't tell.
Whatever you did down there, the graveyard's gone quiet. Thanks for that.
Bandits? Ember lot, red sashes, by the bridge and the gallows trees. I count them, I don't chase them.
Their leader's the one by the bridge, last I counted. Count's my job. Fighting's yours, apparently.
You came back up out of the mill. People don't, lately. You look awful. Good. Means you're alive.
Rats in the Warrens, they say. Big ones. Smart ones. Rats with decks. I hate this job.
The old mill's east, past the chapel. Stairs go down under the wheel. Never been. Never will.
Good luck. I mean it. Mostly I mean please don't make me go and find you.
Gate's open. Moor's out there. Mind the bog and anything that smiles at you.
Not much happens at this gate. That's how I like it. That's how nobody else likes it.
Oh! Sorry. I'm Pell. I light the lamps. Well. I light them when I have oil. Which I don't.
The road's full of Ember Bandits. They take my oil carts. They drink it, I think. Can you drink oil?
Evening round. Twenty-six lamps, one ladder, one Pell. I do the square first so people see me.
The oil's flowing again, thanks to you. Every one of these lamps is a little bit yours.
Before you go to the coast, could you... the bandits? Their leader's still by the bridge. Still my oil.
The coast! Do they have lamps there? Do they need a lamplighter? I'm only asking. I'm not asking.
Every lamp in the square is lit tonight. I did that. You helped. Mostly you did that.
The hall's alight! I lit the square's lamps to match. Wasted half my oil. Worth it.
Elder Hesk sent you to the mill? Take a lamp. Take two. The Warrens eat light.
I'd come with you. I won't. But I'd like you to know I thought about it.
Dark nights are the worst for a lamplighter. People bump into things. Into me, mostly.
Master Orrin said each lamp is a small Accord with the dark. I don't get it. I like it.
So. Orrin's scribe. You have his frown and none of his patience. Good. Patience is wasted on me.
I am Hesk. I keep this town's quarrels and its secrets. Lately the secrets keep me.
You knock at this hour? Orrin did that. Always a question that couldn't wait for morning.
Mine can. Saltmere, scribe. Sleep first. The ferry won't sail any sooner for a tired face.
You're back, and the hall is lit. Sit. Show me what you carried up from that place.
Saltmere is three days by road, two if you don't stop to argue. Orrin always stopped to argue.
The Hush is moving. So should you. Lantern Hollow will keep a lamp lit for you.
You've been under the mill. Did you see him? The Priest? No? Then go deeper.
The dead walk because he tells them a story. Beat his Echoes and the story ends.
The old mill is east, past the chapel. Its cellar stairs go down to the Warrens.
Take your best deck. Take a spare. The Priest does not play fair. He plays forever.
The well's water has gone grey this week. Everything goes grey near the Hush.
Orrin rode north-east a season ago. He promised to write. He wrote once. Then nothing.
Oh! You found me. Nobody finds me. I was told to hide very well.
Don't tell the artist. Here, have a wave. It's all I've got.
Shh. Even hidden people sleep. I sleep hidden. It's very restful until somebody finds me.
The hall's lit, I hear. I'm staying put. The forest's edge is a lovely place to be missed.
Still here. Still hidden. You're very bad at not finding me.
Evening. Or morning. One of those. I'm Bertil, the night watch. The day lad's asleep.
Gate stays open all night. Orders. Nobody said I had to like what comes through it.
Quiet out there now. I almost miss the groaning. Almost.
Ember lot? Red sashes, by the bridge and the gallows trees. They camp out there all night.
Their leader keeps by the bridge, the day lad says. He counts. I just listen for the singing.
You've been down the mill? Then you know what's been crossing my road at night. Rats. Big ones.
The old mill's east, past the chapel. Stairs go down under the wheel. I'd wait for light.
You won't, will you. Nobody does.
Brazier's warm, if you want it. Out there it's just the moor and whatever the moor has got.
I'm Wenna. I sit by the well at night. My brother drew water here, before the Hush.
The dead walk the moor now. I keep hoping one of them is him. Then I hope it isn't.
You took the card from the well. It was my brother's. Keep it. Win something with it.
You left my brother's card where it lay. Thank you. Some things are owed to the dead.
The dead lie still now. I came anyway. Habit is a kind of grief, I think.
You heard the chapel bell? It rings for the ones who won't lie down. Nobody rings it.
The water's grey. Hesk says it's the Hush. I say it's tired, like the rest of us.
The bounty board! Folk pin up the jobs they'd pay to see done.
I keep the book and pay out. Win the duels a job asks for, and come back to me.
Back for your pay? Let's see the board.
Fancy the gauntlet? Three duels, one after another, here in the hall.
Pay the entry and win what you can. A duel lost in here costs you nothing more.
The gauntlet's open. Step up if you have the nerve.
This is the sparring yard. Practice duels here, with nothing riding on them.
I set your deck against the moor's foes, many times over, and count how often it wins.
No gold, no cards, no time lost - just the count.
Back to test your deck? The posts are ready.
